_comment: Canonical GPU capability + dtype-alias table for kernel-set. SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Loaded by models/select.py (the static model->kernel planner) and bindings/python/kernel_set/backends/_probe.py (the runtime dispatch arch/dtype gate). Pure data (stdlib json), no python imports across packages. Add a new GPU arch or dtype alias HERE, not in the python modules.
_sm_doc: sm = compute capability major*10+minor. T4=75, A100=80, A10=86, L4/RTX4090=89, H100/H200/H800=90, Blackwell DC (B200/GB200)=100, consumer Blackwell (RTX50xx)=120. The current optimal table folds sm120 into the sm100 Blackwell capability family.

sm_family_aliases._doc: Raw detected SM -> optimal-table capability-family SM. RTX50/consumer Blackwell reports sm120, but the current provider table keys Blackwell rows as sm100.

sm_thresholds._doc: Minimum SM for each capability. Named so the magic numbers live in one place.

dtype_aliases._doc: Free-form dtype request (or torch.dtype name minus 'torch.') -> short canonical token. Superset shared by select.py (DTYPE_NORMALIZE) and _probe.py (_DTYPE_ALIASES). Note: select.py historically normalized to its own scheme tokens (w4a16/w8a8/mxfp4); _probe.py normalizes to the gate tokens (int4/int8/fp4). Each module maps these canonical tokens to its own vocabulary; see KSCTL_DTYPE_NORMALIZE / PROBE_DTYPE_ALIASES below.

ksctl_dtype_normalize._doc: models/select.py DTYPE_NORMALIZE: requested-dtype token -> internal scheme token. Identity unless listed.

ks_dtype_enum._doc: compute scheme -> ks_dtype_t enum token actually handed to the kernel.

probe_dtype_aliases._doc: bindings/.../backends/_probe.py _DTYPE_ALIASES: torch/free-form dtype -> short gate token (fp16/bf16/fp32/tf32/fp8/int8/int4/fp4).
